recognize_zh: 紅血球之間可見一條細長、規則螺旋捲曲的游離螺旋菌（spirochete），長度約為紅血球直徑的 1–2 倍，位於細胞外，這是回歸熱疏螺旋體（Borrelia）在周邊血液抹片的典型表現。
features: Single thin, loosely coiled, extracellular spirochete lying in the plasma between red cells
Organism length roughly 1-2 red cell diameters with several regular spiral turns
Neutrophil with a band-like/segmented nucleus in the field
Red cells show mild anisocytosis without intracellular parasites
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a thin, helically coiled, extracellular spirochete in the plasma between erythrocytes, measuring approximately one to two red cell diameters in length. A neutrophil is present; red cells show mild anisocytosis without intraerythrocytic inclusions. In the appropriate clinical setting of recurrent fevers, findings are consistent with relapsing fever borreliosis (Borrelia hermsii); organisms are most numerous during febrile episodes and may be missed between them.

ddx.vs: Fibrin strands are straight or branching and irregular, lacking the regular spiral coils and tapered ends of a spirochete.
Microfilariae are much larger (many red cell diameters long) with nuclear columns, not thin spirals.
Trypanosomes are broader, with an undulating membrane, a nucleus, a kinetoplast and a flagellum.
Leptospira are finer, tightly coiled with hooked ends and are rarely visible on Wright-stained blood smears.
